evidence_binding.note: These decisions are valid only against the impact analysis with this exact hash.

decisions.title: Is additive re-branching permitted at all?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: May question eligibility be re-evaluated after an answer, adding newly eligible questions but never withdrawing one?
decisions.affected_paths: 56 (source, option) pairs can unlock a question
decisions.clinical_impact: Can change which symptoms a user ends up declaring, and therefore the scoring input. 30 of 50 conditions are touched.
decisions.product_impact: Users answer more questions on some paths; the flow changes shape mid-assessment.
regression_requirements: re-branching is bounded by the path limit and cannot loop
an assessment with no additional-symptoms answer presents exactly the baseline questions
approval_authorizes: additive re-branching only, subject to the subordinate decisions below
approval_does_not_authorize: any change to the path limit

decisions.title: Is re-branching that unlocks only a severity question permitted?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: Severity answer tokens (mild/moderate/severe/very_severe) carry no scoring weight and no red-flag reference in kb 2.4 or rules 2.2. May a newly eligible severity question be presented?

evidence.caveat: These tokens carry no scoring weight and no red-flag reference IN kb 2.4 AND rules 2.2. That is a property of the CURRENT artifacts, not of the tokens. A future KB revision that gives `severe` or `days_7_plus` a weight would make this subset clinically active with no change to the question flow, so any approval of an inert subset must be re-validated on every clinical artifact change and must be enforced by a validator rather than by this sentence.

decisions.affected_paths: 11 newly triggerable severity questions across the 56 pairs
decisions.clinical_impact: None against the CURRENT artifacts. The tokens appear in no condition's symptoms, no rule, no condition red_flags and no clarifier trigger. This is a property of kb 2.4 and rules 2.2, not of the tokens, and must be re-validated on every clinical artifact change.
decisions.product_impact: One additional question on affected paths.
regression_requirements: a validator asserts severity tokens remain absent from kb, rules, condition red_flags and clarifier triggers
the assertion re-runs on every clinical artifact change
approval_authorizes: presenting a newly eligible severity question
approval_does_not_authorize: treating severity tokens as permanently nonclinical
any scoring change should a future KB give them weight

decisions.title: Is re-branching that unlocks only a duration question permitted?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: Duration answer tokens (days_1_3/days_3_7/days_7_plus/weeks_2_plus) carry no scoring weight and no red-flag reference today. May a newly eligible duration question be presented?

evidence.caveat: These tokens carry no scoring weight and no red-flag reference IN kb 2.4 AND rules 2.2. That is a property of the CURRENT artifacts, not of the tokens. A future KB revision that gives `severe` or `days_7_plus` a weight would make this subset clinically active with no change to the question flow, so any approval of an inert subset must be re-validated on every clinical artifact change and must be enforced by a validator rather than by this sentence.

decisions.affected_paths: 54 newly triggerable duration questions across the 56 pairs
decisions.clinical_impact: None against the CURRENT artifacts, with the same caveat as D002.
decisions.product_impact: One additional question on affected paths.
regression_requirements: a validator asserts duration tokens remain absent from kb, rules, condition red_flags and clarifier triggers
approval_authorizes: presenting a newly eligible duration question
approval_does_not_authorize: treating duration tokens as permanently nonclinical

decisions.title: Is re-branching that makes NEW SCORING TOKENS reachable permitted?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: A newly eligible additional-symptoms question offers options the user could not otherwise declare. 14 such tokens exist, touching 30 of 50 conditions. May they become reachable?

evidence.score_urgency_ranking_delta: NOT COMPUTED — requires the Mobile ScoringEngine. See the handoff for the harness.

decisions.clinical_impact: CHANGES SCORING INPUT. The exact per-condition weight delta is published; the resulting ranked conditions, top condition and urgency are NOT computed here and must be measured in Mobile before this decision is taken.
decisions.product_impact: Users may declare symptoms they would otherwise not have been asked about — arguably better assessment, arguably a longer flow.
regression_requirements: Mobile static-versus-dynamic simulation over the bounded state set, reporting score, ranked conditions, top condition and urgency deltas
approval_authorizes: making the listed tokens reachable through re-branching
approval_does_not_authorize: any change to a token's weight or meaning
activation before the Mobile scoring delta is measured

decisions.title: Does re-branching make any NEW RED FLAG reachable?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: Measured across all four pathways: global rules, condition-specific red_flags, clarifier triggers and clarifier red-flag tokens.

combination_only.basis: rules.ng.v2.2 keys every rule on a SINGLE token; no rule requires a combination. Condition red_flags are also single tokens. There is therefore no combination-only red-flag pathway to model in the current artifacts.

decisions.affected_paths: 0 of 14 newly reachable tokens touch any red-flag pathway
decisions.clinical_impact: NONE MEASURED. No newly reachable token is a global rule token, a condition-specific red flag, a clarifier trigger or a clarifier red-flag token. Had any been, this would be a safety blocker and immediate evaluation after that answer would be mandatory.
regression_requirements: a validator asserts this count stays at zero
QB-002 immediate evaluation remains unconditional and is re-asserted after every re-branch step
approval_authorizes: confirming that no new red flag becomes reachable
approval_does_not_authorize: any relaxation of immediate red-flag evaluation
treating this as permanent — it must be re-measured whenever kb, rules or the clarifier set changes

decisions.title: When re-branching pushes past the limit of 5, what is dropped?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: Grouping collapses each role to one question, so the presented count is bounded at 3 clarifiers + 3 grouped roles = 6, which can exceed 5 by one. Which question yields?

alternatives: A: drop the newest ordinary question (baseline questions win)
B: drop the lowest-priority ordinary question by the existing order key (current truncation rule, unchanged)
C: raise the limit — OUT OF SCOPE, the limit is locked at 5

decisions.affected_paths: Paths where 3 clarifiers are eligible and re-branching adds a role
decisions.clinical_impact: A dropped question is a symptom the user is never asked about. Which one is dropped is a clinical judgement, not a UI preference.
decisions.product_impact: Determines whether the flow feels like it grew or reordered.
regression_requirements: no red-flag question is ever displaced
no required question is silently dropped
the surviving set is deterministic under reversed input

decisions.title: How deep may re-branching recurse?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: The graph has 15 two-cycles and a measured convergence depth of 5. Additive growth terminates, but should the depth be capped below the natural fixed point?
decisions.clinical_impact: A deeper chain means more declarable symptoms; a shallower cap means the flow stops adapting sooner. Both are defensible.
decisions.product_impact: Depth is invisible to the user except as question count.
regression_requirements: convergence is proven within the declared bound

decisions.title: How is progress shown when the flow grows mid-assessment?
decisions.question_for_reviewers: A question added after the user believed they were near the end makes a progress indicator move backwards or become wrong.

evidence.note: Grouping bounds the growth; the UX question is how it is communicated, not how large it is.

decisions.affected_paths: Any path where re-branching adds a question
decisions.clinical_impact: None directly. A misleading indicator can cause abandonment, which is a safety-adjacent outcome — the QB-002 finding was abandonment, not under-triage.
decisions.product_impact: Product owns the indicator design. This analysis does not propose a UI.
regression_requirements: abandonment measurement before and after, if activated
approval_does_not_authorize: any change to question content or order

path_length_analysis.note: Grouping is what keeps this small. Without contract 1.1 each newly eligible question would consume its own slot and the limit of 5 would bind hard; with grouping the presented count is bounded at 3 clarifiers + 3 grouped roles.

ux_analysis.repeated_or_redundant_questions: None: grouping presents one question per role, and answering an option for a token already in state is idempotent (S09).
ux_analysis.user_visible_branch_transitions: A new question can appear after an additional-symptoms answer.

case_bank_applicability.limitation: Every case supplies a FINAL token set, not a question-and-answer sequence. IM-003 is a property of the sequence — which answer unlocked which question — so the bank cannot exercise it. No sequence was invented, and the 239-case suite is NOT claimed to validate adaptive branching.
case_bank_applicability.what_the_bank_does_still_prove: That the clinical baseline is unchanged by this analysis, because no runtime artifact was modified.

options_considered.C: Permit additive scoring-affecting branching after clinical approval.
options_considered.D: Require a revised question/content model first.

decomposition_recommendation.engineering_recommendation: B with conditions, then C separately. The evidence supports a clean split that is STRUCTURALLY enforceable rather than a prose convention: a newly eligible question whose answer tokens carry no scoring weight and no red-flag reference (severity and duration today) is clinically inert against the current artifacts, while a newly eligible additional-symptoms question makes new scoring tokens reachable and is not. The two have different risk and should not share one approval.

structural_enforcement.mechanism: The split must be enforced by the artifact and a validator, not by reviewer discipline. The proposed shape is a per-question declaration — for example a `rebranch_class` of `inert` or `scoring_affecting` — COMPUTED by the generator from the token's clinical references and re-validated on every clinical artifact change, so a KB revision that gives `severe` a weight reclassifies the question automatically instead of silently invalidating an approval.
structural_enforcement.not_proposed_here: No schema change is made in this step. The shape above is a recommendation for a future step to design and review.

decomposition_recommendation.why_not_A: Deferring everything indefinitely leaves a known defect — a flow that cannot react to its own answers — unaddressed, and the inert subset carries no measured clinical risk.
decomposition_recommendation.why_not_C_yet: The scoring-affecting subset changes the scoring input on 30 of 50 conditions and its score/urgency/ranking delta has NOT been measured, because that requires the Mobile engine. Approving it before that measurement would be approving an unquantified change to triage input.
decomposition_recommendation.why_not_D: Nothing in the evidence shows the question or content model is wrong. The questions, answers and token effects are unchanged and correct; the gap is behavioural, not structural.
